content: Curb your desires, don't set your heart on so many things and you will get what you need.
author: Epictetus
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

Across his life and work, Epictetus saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
